newsitem.title: USA: U.S. resident held in Cuba over explosive - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. resident held in Cuba over explosive - report.

text.p: Cuban police have detained a woman from Hialeah, Florida, for allegedly bringing into Cuba the same kind of plastic explosives reportedly used in recent bombings on the island, the Miami Herald said on Wednesday.
The Herald said the woman was a 35-year-old legal U.S. resident from Cuba but did not give her name, saying it had been asked not to do so in order not to complicate efforts to win her release.

Cuban security officials say they found C-4, a putty-like plastic explosive, in her shoulder bag soon after she arrived in Havana in early May for her annual one-week visit with a brother, the newspaper said, quoting an unnamed family friend.
The newspaper said the same plastic explosive had been used in a bombing at the five-star Melia Cohiba hotel in Havana in mid-April, causing damage but no injuries.
A U.S. official said Washington has asked Havana about the reports and the Cuban government has said it does not have any Americans detained in connection with any alleged bombings.

Diplomats in Havana believe at least one bomb went off and one was deactivated in Cuba this year. Cuban authorities, who have not confirmed the alleged bombings, were not immediately available to comment on Wednesday on the latest report.

The Herald quoted the woman's friends as saying she was not politically active. They said she was unaware of any explosives and that they might have been hidden in thick envelopes of letters and photos that co-workers asked her to deliver to contacts in Havana during a visit last month.
If the woman is a Cuban resident of the United States and not a U.S. citizen, U.S. authorities cannot formally intercede on her behalf.

Quoting the friend, the Herald said Cuban security agents questioned the woman's brother in Havana and inspected his car for traces of explosives but found nothing. The newspaper also said the woman's husband, who is in Florida, has hired a defence lawyer in Havana.
It said the woman's detention brought to six the number of people held by Cuban police in connection with the bombs. Hialeah, just outside Miami, is home to many Cuban-Americans.
